newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific Resources outlook positive.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific Resources outlook positive.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group Inc on Wednesday reported record first quarter production and said its outlook is very positive despite the recent decline in oil and natural gas prices.

It said average daily volumes from producing properties increased 17 percent over the first quarter of 1996 to 1.61 billion cubic feet equivalent per day, adding that this was an all-time quarterly record and the fourth consecutive quarter in which a new volume record was reached.
Total sales volumes, which include producing properties and gas plants, averaged 1.88 billion cubic feet daily.
The company noted that was an increase of 16 percent.
It said first quarter earnings increased 98 percent to $117.2 million on a 36 precent increase in revenues to $531.7 million.
Discretionary cash flow -- the sum of net income; depreciation, depletion and amortization; exploration expenses; and deferred taxes -- was up 46 percent to $321.1 million.
"We were very successful in the first quarter and achieved our best quarter ever, excluding the fourth quarter of 1995, when a large settlement was recorded," chief executive Jack L. Messman said.

"Despite the recent decline in oil and gas prices, our outlook is very positive. With 60 percent of our 1997 oil and gas volumes hedged at prices favorable to the current market, we have reduced our downside exposure to prices," he said.
Union Pacific Resoures said it now has 55 operated rigs drilling compared with 35 running on a daily basis, on average, in the second quarter of 1996.

It said this includes three operated rigs drilling in the Cotton Valley Pinnacle Reef trend in East Texas. The wells --the Lightning, the Thunderbolt and the Bearcat -- are 100 percent Union Pacific wells until payout and should reach their target objective in the second quarter.
The company said it also has an interest in two nonoperated Cotton Valley Pinnacle Reef wells which are currently drilling.

It said the Masters Creek Gas plant, which will process 100 million cubic feet of high BTU natural gas daily in the Louisiana extension of the Austin Chalk, is expected to begin operations in the second quarter.
Construction will continue after plant start-up in order to expand the capacity of the plant by 100 percent to 200 million cubic feet per day.
